title: The 132 Pattern

concept.title: Scan from the right and remember the best "2"
body: A **132 pattern** is a triple of positions `i < j < k` with `a[i] < a[k] < a[j]` (the values look like "1", "3", "2"). Checking all triples is O(n^3). With a monotonic stack and a scan **from the right** it takes O(n).

Call `a[k]` the "2" and `a[j]` the "3". Keep a stack of candidates for the "3", with decreasing values, and a variable `third`, the **largest value that has been used as a "2"** (it was popped from the stack by a bigger element, so a bigger "3" stands to its left). When you reach a new element `x`: if `x < third`, then `x` can be the "1" and the pattern exists. Otherwise pop all stack elements smaller than `x`; the last popped one is a new, larger "2" candidate (`x` is a bigger "3" for it); then push `x`.

body.code:
third = -inf; stack = []
for x in reversed(a):
    if x < third: return True               # x is the "1"
    while stack and stack[-1] < x:
        third = stack.pop()                 # a candidate for the "2", with x as its "3"
    stack.append(x)
return False

body: Why the **largest** such value is kept: the test `x < third` is easier to pass when `third` is larger. A larger "2" candidate is always valid, because it was popped by a bigger element standing to its left, which can play the "3".

statement: Given an array, is there a triple of positions `i < j < k` with `a[i] < a[k] < a[j]`? Print `yes` or `no`.

examples.note: The values 1, 4, 2 (at positions 2, 3, 4) form a 132 pattern.

hints: A brute force over triples is too slow.
Go from the right. Keep a stack of decreasing values and the best value `third` that was popped.
If the current value is smaller than `third`, a pattern exists.

explanation: Scanning from the right, `third` is the largest value that has a larger value to its left among the processed ones. Any later (more to the left) element smaller than `third` completes a 132 pattern.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

third = None
stack = []
found = False
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    x = a[i]
    if third is not None and x < third:
        found = True
        break
    while stack and stack[-1] < x:
        third = stack.pop()
    stack.append(x)
print("yes" if found else "no")
